### Problem: serialize and deserialize a binary tree {#sec-tv-p5-codec}

::: {.p-statement}
Design a codec that turns a binary tree into a string and the string back into the same tree. There is no restriction on the format.

Constraints: up to $10^4$ nodes, values in $[-1000, 1000]$.

Source: [LC 297 · Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree/){.solved difficulty="Hard"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
A preorder with a `#` for every missing child is enough. The left subtree's tokens are a prefix of what remains, so the recursive decode of the left child returns with the index already sitting on the right child. An empty tree is the single token `#`.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Recursive preorder.** Append values and `#`, join with commas. Decode splits and walks with one index.
2. **Explicit stack.** The same string. Encode pushes right, then left, including nulls. Decode keeps `(node, how many children are filled)` and attaches the next token to the first node that still has a free slot.

**Invariant.** After `decode` returns a subtree, the shared index is the first token that does not belong to that subtree. Level order is a second codec: emit both child slots of every node, `#` when a child is missing, and decode with a queue. `[1,2,3]` is then `1,2,3,#,#,#,#`, while the marked preorder is `1,2,#,#,3,#,#`.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Preorder

::: {.form-next}
Build the string in a list. Concatenating a string at every node copies the whole prefix.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("ser", "pre")
    assert str(final) == "1,2,#,#,3,4,#,#,5,#,#"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def serialize(root):
    out = []

    def enc(u):
        if u is None:
            out.append("#")
            return
        out.append(str(u.val))
        enc(u.left)
        enc(u.right)

    enc(root)
    return ",".join(out)


def deserialize(data):
    tok = data.split(",")
    i = 0

    def dec():
        nonlocal i
        t = tok[i]
        i += 1
        if t == "#":
            return None
        node = Node(int(t))
        node.left = dec()
        node.right = dec()
        return node

    return dec()
```

##### C++

```cpp
string serialize(TreeNode* u) {
    if (!u) return "#";
    return to_string(u->val) + "," + serialize(u->left) + "," + serialize(u->right);
}
```

:::

#### Stack

::: {.form-next}
The same tokens, written and read without a call stack. A path of $10^4$ nodes is comfortable here and tight as recursion.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("ser", "stack")
    assert str(final) == "1,2,#,#,3,4,#,#,5,#,#"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def serialize_stack(root):
    out, st = [], [root]
    while st:
        u = st.pop()
        if u is None:
            out.append("#")
            continue
        out.append(str(u.val))
        st.append(u.right)
        st.append(u.left)
    return ",".join(out)


sample = from_level([1, 2, 3, None, None, 4, 5])
text = "1,2,#,#,3,4,#,#,5,#,#"
assert serialize(sample) == serialize_stack(sample) == text
assert to_level(deserialize(text)) == [1, 2, 3, None, None, 4, 5]
assert serialize(None) == "#"
assert deserialize("#") is None
left = from_level([1, 2])
right = from_level([1, None, 2])
assert serialize(left) == "1,2,#,#,#"
assert serialize(right) == "1,#,2,#,#"
assert to_level(deserialize(serialize(left))) == [1, 2]
assert to_level(deserialize(serialize(right))) == [1, None, 2]
```

##### C++

```cpp
// Stack preorder: push the right child, then the left, and push nulls too.
// Each null is the token "#". Decode with a stack of (node, children filled).
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
$O(n)$ time either way. The string holds $n$ values and $n + 1$ markers. Recursion uses $O(h)$ stack. The explicit stack uses $O(h)$ heap memory.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- The empty tree is `#`, not `""`.
- `[1,2]` is `1,2,#,#,#`. `[1,null,2]` is `1,#,2,#,#`. Dropping the markers makes them the same string.
- The index must be shared. A copy of the index lets the right subtree restart inside the left subtree.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- `[1,2]` and `[1,null,2]` are both the preorder `1, 2` once the markers are dropped.
- An index passed by value makes both children start on the same token. One shared index walks the whole string.
- Reading a value one character at a time breaks on $-1000$. Split on the comma, then convert the token.
:::

**Variants.** Parentheses are this preorder: an empty left child is `()` when a right child follows, and a missing right child is omitted. A BST with distinct values stores the preorder alone and decodes with a value range. An N-ary node can store its value and the number of children.
